method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

Automated screening compared source references, locators, geography fields, evidence class, direction, status, horizon and scenario; it checked pathway support IDs, link-evidence sets, geography fields, alternatives and uncertainty for follow-up.

Raw extraction access rows are recorded only as inherited access observations. This generated screen does not treat snippets, HTTP success, prior access, or metadata as claim verification and does not replace semantic source review.

source_refs.locator: CCDR, Executive Summary, printed p. 7, and chapter 1, printed pp. 22–24, regional water, land and flood risks

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11 reports: Flood losses relative to regional GDP are highest in Vayots Dzor, Tavush, Lori and Gegharkunik; the report also locates severe irrigation-water and land-degradation risks in high-poverty marzes.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: CCDR, chapter 1, printed p. 20, spatial disparities and fragility risks

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-11 reports: The CCDR links spatial disparities with fragility risks, notes high rural and border-region poverty, and says conflict with Azerbaijan raises risks across the economy; it does not identify climate change as causing conflict.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Fourth National Communication, printed pp. 93–94, satellite-based severe-drought damage frequency, 1984–2017

evidence.compact_statement: The 2020 communication's satellite-based assessment for 1984–2017 describes differentiated drought-related crop damage in the Ararat Valley, southwestern Gegharkunik, Kotayk and Gegharkunik. Its damage-frequency categories are not reused as current annual probabilities.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Fourth National Communication, printed pp. 93–94, Tables 5-7 to 5-9, yield projections by marz

evidence.scenario: The yield tables describe climate-change projections without agrotechnical measures but do not identify the emissions pathway.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020 reports: By 2070, projected wheat yields fall about 19–20% in Ararat, Kotayk and Gegharkunik, potato yields 21% in Shirak, while wheat yields rise about 8% in Lori.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: Fourth National Communication, printed p. 138, pilot crop-insurance program

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020 reports: The communication records a crop-insurance pilot launched in 2018: potatoes and cereals against hail and frost in Shirak, and fruit and grapes in Armavir and Ararat.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: National Action Program, printed pp. 10–11, barriers to adaptation

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The NAP identifies weak inter-agency coordination and information flows, poor climate integration in public bodies, and gaps in locally relevant risk data and local adaptation finance.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: National Action Program, printed pp. 30–32, measures 1.9–1.10 for marz adaptation plans

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The 2021–2025 action list scheduled adaptation plans for pilot marzes Shirak and Tavush, then eight more marzes, integrating climate adaptation into regional development planning.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: National Action Program, printed p. 19, principle on gender-responsive adaptation

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2021-05-13 reports: The NAP says social norms can restrict women’s access to climate information, resources and opportunities, and calls for gender-responsive participation in adaptation decisions.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

source_refs.locator: UNSDCF, printed pp. 23–24, climate risks and potential displacement in the framework rationale

evidence.scenario: UNSDCF 2026–2030 planning horizon; no climate scenario or displacement estimate is stated.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-12-19 reports: The framework includes possible displacement among the human impacts of climate risks and places climate adaptation within a wider resilience and social-cohesion agenda.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.
